newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat harvest 97 percent complete.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat harvest 97 percent complete.

text.p: Harvesting of Oklahoma's wheat crop was 97 percent complete as of Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop progress report.
Harvesting was on par with the five-year average of 97 percent but was slightly behind 100 percent last year.
"Harvest was virtually complete with most of the wheat remaining for harvest in the south central distict and across the northern tier of counties," the report said.
The report said that while some areas received rain, soil moisture levels were at their lowest rating since late March.
Corn was rated 93 percent in good to excellent condition, ahead of 86 percent in that category a week ago.
Sorghum was rated 76 percent in good to excellent condition, against 74 percent at that level last week. Sorghum was 78 percent up to stand, behind 98 percent last year and 91 percent on average.
Cotton was rated 77 percent in good to excellent condition, above 68 percent at that level last week. Cotton was 49 percent squaring, lagging 81 percent last year and 54 percent on average.
